title: Mauritius at a glance
summary: The short answers about Mauritius in one place: where it is, which islands make up the Republic, its size and population, the capital, how it is governed, its languages, money and time, the flag and the national day. Figures are the latest official ones read on 20 November 2026.
audience: Anyone who wants the basic facts about Mauritius: students, visitors, people moving here and people doing business with the island.

facts.label: Population
facts.detail: Provisional mid-year estimate for the Republic. The 2022 census counted 1,233,427 residents.

facts.label: Land area
facts.detail: Island of Mauritius 1,868.4 km², Rodrigues 110.1 km², Agalega 26.0 km² and St Brandon 2.7 km².

facts.label: Capital
facts.detail: In the north-west of the main island.

facts.label: National day
facts.detail: Independence Day and Republic Day. Independence came on 12 March 1968 and the Republic on 12 March 1992.

facts.label: Currency
facts.detail: Only the Bank of Mauritius may issue notes and coins.

facts.label: Time zone
facts.detail: The law sets standard time as the solar time of longitude 60 degrees east of Greenwich.

facts.label: Language most spoken at home
facts.detail: Alone or with another language. 78.6% spoke only Creole. English is the official language of the National Assembly.

facts.label: Driving
facts.detail: Drivers give way to vehicles coming from the right.

facts.label: Dialling code
facts.detail: Fixed numbers have 7 digits and mobile numbers 8.

facts.label: Internet domain
facts.detail: A country-code top-level domain. Its manager is Internet Direct Ltd of Port Louis.

blocks.text: Mauritius is an island state in the south-west of the Indian Ocean, about 2,000 km from the east coast of Africa. The main island lies just inside the Tropic of Capricorn, at 20° south and 57° east. It is of volcanic origin and almost entirely surrounded by coral reefs. Together with Réunion and Rodrigues it forms the group of islands known as the Mascarenes.

The land rises from the coastal plain to a central plateau that reaches 670 metres and is bordered by three mountain ranges. The highest peak is Piton de la Rivière Noire at 826 metres, ahead of Pieter Both at 818 metres and Le Pouce at 811 metres. The climate is maritime, tropical in summer and subtropical in winter. Summer runs from October to March and winter from June to September.

sections.heading: Which islands make up the Republic of Mauritius?

blocks.text: The Republic is more than one island. The Constitution says that Mauritius includes the islands of Mauritius, Rodrigues, Agalega, Tromelin, Cargados Carajos and the Chagos Archipelago, including Diego Garcia, and any other island comprised in the State of Mauritius. Cargados Carajos is more often called St Brandon.

rows: The main island, with the capital, Port Louis
About 580 km to the north-east, with its own Regional Assembly
Two islands about 1,000 km north of Mauritius
A group of islets about 450 km to the north-north-east, mainly fishing outposts
Statistics Mauritius gives no area or count for Tromelin or the Chagos Archipelago

blocks.text: Agalega is administered by the Outer Islands Development Corporation, which comes under the Prime Minister's Office. In its Act the Outer Islands are all the islands of the State other than Mauritius and Rodrigues.

The Chagos Archipelago has been administered by the United Kingdom. In an advisory opinion of 25 February 2019 the International Court of Justice concluded that the United Kingdom was under an obligation to end that administration as rapidly as possible. On 22 May 2025 the two governments signed an agreement which states that Mauritius is sovereign over the archipelago in its entirety, including Diego Garcia.

sections.heading: How big is Mauritius and how many people live there?

blocks.text: The land area of the Republic is 2,007.2 km², of which the island of Mauritius takes 1,868.4 km². Statistics Mauritius estimated the population at 1,240,316 on 1 July 2026: 1,194,974 on the island of Mauritius, 45,012 on Rodrigues and 330 on Agalega and St Brandon. That is 618 people for each square kilometre.

The last census, taken in July 2022, counted 1,233,427 residents. Leaving out Agalega, the count was 3,720 lower than in 2011, the first fall from one census to the next since 1911. The yearly estimates run a little higher than the census because they add an allowance for young children the census missed.

sections.heading: What is the capital, and how is Mauritius governed?

blocks.text: The capital is Port Louis. Mauritius is a sovereign democratic State known as the Republic of Mauritius. It became independent on 12 March 1968 and a Republic on 12 March 1992.

Parliament is made up of the President and a National Assembly of up to 70 members. The President is the Head of State, elected by the Assembly for five years. The Prime Minister is the member of the Assembly who appears to the President best able to command the support of a majority. In November 2026 the President is Dharambeer Gokhool, in office since 7 December 2024, and the Prime Minister is Dr Navinchandra Ramgoolam.

sections.heading: What languages are spoken, and what money is used?

blocks.text: The Constitution does not name a national language. Its one rule on an official language is for Parliament: English is the official language of the National Assembly, and any member may address the chair in French. At home the language is Creole, which official papers now call Kreol Morisien. At the 2022 census 89.9% of residents said they usually spoke it at home, alone or with another language.
The unit of currency is the rupee, which is divided into 100 cents. The Bank of Mauritius has the sole right to issue notes and coins.

items: Time: Mauritius is four hours ahead of Greenwich, UTC +4. The law fixes standard time as the solar time of longitude 60 degrees east.
Driving: on the left, giving way to vehicles coming from the right.
Telephone: the international dialling code is +230. Fixed numbers have 7 digits and mobile numbers 8.
Electricity: 220/230 V, with British three-square-pin plugs and two-round-pin plugs.

sections.heading: What do the flag and the national symbols stand for?

blocks.text: The flag has four equal horizontal stripes of red, blue, yellow and green, and is in the proportion of 6 to 4. The Government gives each colour a meaning.

items: Red represents the struggle for freedom and independence.
Blue represents the Indian Ocean, in the middle of which Mauritius is situated.
Yellow represents the new light of independence shining over the island.
Green represents the agriculture of Mauritius and its colour throughout the twelve months of the year.

blocks.text: The coat of arms is supported by a dodo and a sambur deer, each holding a sugar cane, above the motto Stella Clavisque Maris Indici. The national anthem opens with the words Glory to thee, Motherland. Its words are by the poet Jean Georges Prosper and its music by Philippe Gentil of the Police Band. The national flower, since 12 March 1992, is Trochetia boutoniana, known as Boucle d'Oreille.

12 March is Independence Day and Republic Day, a public holiday every year. Two more fixed holidays recall the island's history: the Abolition of Slavery on 1 February and the Arrival of Indentured Labourers on 2 November. The other public holidays are New Year on 1 and 2 January, Labour Day on 1 May, Christmas on 25 December and the main festivals of the island's religions, whose dates change each year.

The land area and any population of Tromelin and of the Chagos Archipelago. They are named in the Constitution but do not appear in the Statistics Mauritius tables that were read.
Who administers Tromelin today. The Constitution lists it as part of Mauritius. No official page on its present administration was read.

Whether the agreement of 22 May 2025 on the Chagos Archipelago has entered into force. The copy published by the United Kingdom in May 2025 was marked as not in force, and no later official notice was found.
The exact distance from Mauritius to Rodrigues. The tourism authority gives around 580 km to the north-east. No Statistics Mauritius or Rodrigues Regional Assembly page giving the distance was found.
The designer of the flag and the date it was first raised. The Government page on the flag gives neither.
An official English translation of the motto Stella Clavisque Maris Indici. The Government page gives the Latin only.
Whether Mauritius ever changes its clocks. The pages read give UTC +4 and say nothing of summer time.
